**6B.2 Research Note**

Verdict: mixed, leaning yes on targeted access and social protection, but no on broad universal improvement. The strongest 2024 evidence shows expanded cash transfers, education and refugee-service initiatives, and some infrastructure-focused reform. The strongest contrary evidence shows major access failures for refugees and a health policy move that Amnesty said would reduce affordability and access.

- [World Bank Group Statement of Support to Egypt’s Development and Reform Efforts](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/statement/2024/03/18/world-bank-group-statement-of-support-to-egypt-s-development-and-reform-efforts) | World Bank Group | 2024-03-18 | The Bank said the 2024 agenda was aimed at inclusive growth, human capital, resilience, and protection of the poorest and most vulnerable, which is direct support for better access to basic welfare goods. IDs: 6B.2, 6B.1, 5B.10, 5B.9.

- [PR 2459: Egypt staff and authorities reach agreement on reviews under the EFF arrangement](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/03/06/pr-2459-egypt-staff-and-authorities-reach-agreement-on-reviews-under-the-eff-arrangement) | IMF | 2024-03-06 | The IMF said authorities agreed to more social spending for vulnerable groups and a larger cash-transfer package, which is direct evidence of expanded social protection. IDs: 6B.2, 6B.1, 5B.9, 5B.10.

- [Promoting Inclusive Human Capital Development and Building Resilience in Egypt through Cash Transfer Programs](https://www.worldbank.org/en/results/2024/05/28/promoting-inclusive-human-capital-development-and-building-resilience-in-egypt-through-cash-transfer-programs) | World Bank | 2024-05-28 | Takaful and Karama was described as institutionalized and well-targeted, linked to health, education, child nutrition, and women’s empowerment, with a benefit increase to cushion inflation. This is the clearest positive evidence for access to basic welfare and social protection. IDs: 6B.2, 6B.1, 5B.8.

- [Arab Republic of Egypt: Technical Assistance Report: Public Investment Management Assessment](https://www.imf.org/en/publications/technical-assistance-reports/issues/2024/04/02/arab-republic-of-egypt-technical-assistance-report-public-investment-management-assessment-547051) | IMF | 2024-04-02 | The IMF said Egypt had begun improving infrastructure access and public investment management and explicitly referenced Education 2.0 and health-infrastructure rollout. This is evidence of welfare-relevant state capacity building, though still process evidence. IDs: 6B.2, 5B.9, 5B.10, 5B.6.

- [New World Bank US$700 Million Support to Help Egypt Achieve More Sustainable, Diversified and Resilient Growth](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/06/24/new-world-bank-us-700-million-support-to-help-egypt-achieve-more-sustainable-diversified-and-resilient-growth) | World Bank Group | 2024-06-24 | The new DPF supported lower electricity-distribution losses, water and sanitation sustainability, renewables, and stronger SOE governance. That is strong evidence for access-oriented infrastructure and public-service improvement, especially water and sanitation. IDs: 6B.2, 5B.6, 5B.7, 5B.10.

- [Education Cannot Wait, UNHCR, UNICEF and Strategic Partners Call for Increased Resources for the Education Response in Egypt and Region](https://www.unhcr.org/eg/news/education-cannot-wait-unhcr-unicef-strategic-partners-call-increased-resources) | UNHCR Egypt | 2024-08-22 | The joint statement said the government had taken notable steps to provide refugees access to education services, even though needs still exceeded resources. This is a real but partial positive for basic-service access. IDs: 6B.2, 6B.1, 5B.8.

- [Launch of the Joint UN Programme under the Joint Platform for Migrants and Refugees in Egypt](https://www.unhcr.org/eg/news/launch-joint-un-programme-under-joint-platform-migrants-and-refugees-egypt) | UNHCR Egypt | 2024-09-30 | The government, UN, and EU launched a program supporting health and education for refugees and migrants in vulnerable situations. This is direct evidence of expanded access for a clearly vulnerable group. IDs: 6B.2, 6B.1, 5B.8.

- [Egypt new law threatens to reduce access to healthcare for millions](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/07/egypt-new-law-threatens-to-reduce-access-to-healthcare-for-millions/) | Amnesty International | 2024-07-30 | Amnesty said Law 87 of 2024 privatized management of public health facilities without price regulation and was rushed through without adequate consultation. That is contrary evidence on health access and affordability. IDs: 6B.2, 5B.9, 5B.7.

- [Egypt education restricted for refugees](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/12/02/egypt-education-restricted-for-refugees) | Human Rights Watch | 2024-12-02 | HRW found tens of thousands of refugee and asylum-seeking children out of school because of residency bureaucracy, costs, discrimination, and limited free public education. This is strong evidence against broad, equitable access. IDs: 6B.2, 6B.1, 5B.8.

- [Egypt authorities must end campaign of mass arrests and forced returns of Sudanese refugees](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/06/egypt-authorities-must-end-campaign-of-mass-arrests-and-forced-returns-of-sudanese-refugees/) | Amnesty International | 2024-06-19 | Amnesty documented mass arrests, cruel detention conditions, and forced returns of Sudanese refugees without asylum access. That is direct evidence of failed protection for a vulnerable group. IDs: 6B.2, 6B.1, 5B.8.

Search gap: I found strong evidence on cash transfers, education, health infrastructure, and refugee services, but much weaker direct 2024 evidence on housing access, sanitation outcomes at household level, and food-security outcomes beyond the nutrition-linked framing of Takaful/Karama.
